However, it remains open if it is sufficient. We provide the following partial results. Firstly, by a simple inductive argument based on Theorem 12, we show that multi-step probability spaces induced by Markov chains are same-set hitting. Secondly, we show that P is same-set hitting if α(P) > 0 and its correlation ρ(P) is smaller than 1. statement: Theorem 13 requires that ρ < 1 in order to give a meaningful bound. It is unclear whether this is an artifact of our proof or if it is necessary. In particular, consider the three step distribution P which picks a uniform triple from {000, 111, 222, 012, 120, 201}. One easily checks that ρ(P) = 1 and that all marginals are uniform. We do not know if this distribution is same-set hitting.
